seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Antioch, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Antioch, CA: Holiday Delites parade and Waldie Plaza tree lighting, Hope With Lights, Santa's sleigh in Rivertown and BART to Antioch.
lede: Antioch celebrates Christmas in historic Downtown Rivertown, where the city's Holiday Delites parade ends at Waldie Plaza for the tree lighting, and neighbors keep their own traditions of light shows and Santa photos going all season.
celebrates: The big night is Holiday Delites, run by the City of Antioch Recreation Department in Downtown Rivertown. The Downtown Antioch Association fills G Street with a block party of local shops and vendor booths, a lighted parade rolls along W 3rd and W 2nd Streets, and the city tree is lit in Waldie Plaza beside the river. Santa and the Grinch pose for photos and school bands and choirs sing carols. Away from downtown, the nonprofit Hope With Lights ministry runs a nightly Christmas light show with Toy Drive nights, and Willow Park Mercantile on G Street brings Santa in an antique sleigh for photos.
lastyear: On Saturday, December 6, 2025, Antioch held Holiday Delites in 46 degree weather in downtown Rivertown, the Antioch Herald reported. The day began with a Sip and Shop on G Street. Before the tree lighting, city staff handed children STEM kits while families took photos with Santa and the Grinch. Mayor Ron Bernal led the countdown, then the Deer Valley Choir and the Antioch and Deer Valley High School Marching Bands played carols. Santa rode in the Antioch Historical Society's old fire truck, and Delta Veterans Group won Best Decorated.
facts: Antioch is one of California's oldest towns. Brothers William and Joseph Smith settled at Smith's Landing in 1850, and Joseph died of malaria that February. At a town picnic on July 4, 1851, William persuaded residents to rename the town Antioch, after the biblical city where followers of Christ were first called Christians, in memory of his brother. The city incorporated in 1872. Holiday Delites still ends in Rivertown, the old riverfront downtown where the town began.
trains: BART reached Antioch on May 26, 2018, when a 10 mile extension from Pittsburg/Bay Point opened two new stations, Pittsburg Center and Antioch. Antioch station sits in the median of Highway 4 at Hillcrest Avenue, with its entrance at 1600 Slatten Ranch Road. Amtrak also stops in town at its unstaffed Antioch-Pittsburg station, 100 I Street, which opened in 1984. Coal trains once ran here too: the building that served as the Antioch terminus of the old coal railroad still stands at F and Fourth Streets.

Parade entries are judged across from City Hall, with trophies such as Best Decorated, Best Performance and Most Spirited.

kidfact: Antioch got its name at a Fourth of July picnic in 1851. The townspeople voted to name it after an old city in the Bible, to remember a founder who had died.
faq: Where is the Antioch Christmas tree lighting?

The City of Antioch lights its tree in Waldie Plaza in historic Downtown Rivertown during Holiday Delites, right after the lighted parade finishes on W 2nd Street. In 2025 Mayor Ron Bernal led the countdown, and school choirs and marching bands played carols after the tree was lit. The city notes that a heavy downpour cancels the parade and tree lighting.

The City of Antioch Recreation Department runs Holiday Delites, with the parade, tree lighting and Santa photos at Waldie Plaza. The Downtown Antioch Association hosts the block party on G Street with local businesses and vendor booths. Sponsors listed by the city include Republic Services, The Learning Experience and Sunrun.
Can we take BART to Antioch for Christmas events?

Yes. BART's Antioch station opened on May 26, 2018, in the median of Highway 4 at Hillcrest Avenue, with its entrance at 1600 Slatten Ranch Road. It is the end of the line that runs through Pittsburg Center and Pittsburg/Bay Point. Amtrak trains also stop at the Antioch-Pittsburg station at 100 I Street.
Where can kids see Christmas lights in Antioch?

Hope With Lights, a nonprofit ministry on Belvedere Way, runs a Christmas Light Show every night from late November into early January and says its events are free. On its Toy Drive nights, visitors bring new toys and children can take pictures with Santa.
How did Antioch get its name?

Brothers William and Joseph Smith founded Smith's Landing in 1850. After Joseph died, William persuaded residents at a July 4, 1851 picnic to rename the town Antioch, for the biblical city where followers of Christ were first called Christians. The Antioch Historical Museum tells the story of the town's early days.
